evals.prompt: The Stop hook says: Time review needed: this turn spent 9m10s in tools. Slowest steps: npm run verify 6m2s, bats <path> 2m5s, git push 30s. Write the time review.
evals.expected_output: A Time review of at most 5 lines that quotes the hook numbers, names one concrete speedup for npm run verify, and says whether it recurs and whether a task was filed.
expectations: Runs or cites agent-perf.mjs report --session latest (or the 7-day report) before claiming recurrence
Keeps the Time review to 5 lines or fewer
Names one concrete speedup with the step key and an expected saving
States whether the step recurs and either files a task or says Filed: none (one-off)

evals.prompt: What took longest in this repo this week, and what can we speed up?
evals.expected_output: Uses agent-perf.mjs report --days 7, ranks steps by total time (topKeys), reads p50 against p95 and failures, and proposes one concrete speedup.
expectations: Ranks by total time per step rather than by the single slowest call
Mentions the p50 versus p95 gap or failures by step when they are present
Proposes exactly one speedup and quotes report numbers rather than estimates

evals.prompt: Run the agent time part of the tooling checkup across all projects.
evals.expected_output: Uses report --all --days 7 --json plus the session-report analyzer for tokens and hours, lists the top slow recurring steps per project, and files tasks only for speedups of a minute or more that recur.
expectations: Uses the session-report analyze-sessions.mjs --json --since 7d for tokens or hours when it is installed
Files a task only when the speedup saves at least 1 minute and the step recurs
Task text names the step key, the 7-day count and total, the change, and the expected saving

evals.prompt: How many tokens did I spend on this project last week?
evals.expected_output: Points to the session-report skill or analyzer for tokens and cost instead of the perf log, which has no token data.
expectations: Says the perf log records tool time, not tokens
Uses or recommends the session-report analyzer for token and cost numbers
Does not invent token numbers from agent-perf output

evals.prompt: The Stop hook says: Time review needed: 4 tool calls never ran this turn (permission prompt, hook block, or denial): cd <path> 3x, Edit:ts 1x. Write the time review.
evals.expected_output: A Time review of at most 5 lines that names the blocked calls, explains that each cost a round trip, and gives one concrete fix such as splitting the compound cd command into simple Bash calls.
expectations: Quotes the blocked count and the step keys from the hook or from agent-perf.mjs report --session latest
Keeps the Time review to 5 lines or fewer
Names one concrete fix for the top blocked key (split the compound Bash command, or meet the hook gate first)
States whether it recurs and either files a task or says Filed: none (one-off)
